dial.summary: 5/8 indicators supportive entering November 13 — DXY surging to a 52-week high at 103.19 on sustained hot-CPI repricing is the primary headwind, but ISM Manufacturing at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion), Global M2 trending up at $104.3T, real yields easing on a 4-week basis to 2.78%, and BTC funding neutral at 0.0098% sustain the accumulation backdrop; BTC's 4.3% intraday drop reflects DXY pressure rather than a macro breakdown, with BTC.D firm at ~59% and no alt-rotation signal.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) holds at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317B); October G4 data not yet published — MacroMicro typically updates mid-month following the reference month, so October G4 update expected mid-November 2026; US M2 at $23.4T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per Macrotrends/FRED); 4-week Aug→Sep change +$0.64T (+0.6%) exceeds flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged from Nov 11 run — October G4 data publication pending mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.6%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0, New Orders 55.5, Prices Paid 75.2 (down from September's 77.9; still elevated but easing), Employment 52.4; ISM survey chair cited Iran war and price volatility as headwinds despite sustained expansion; 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value unchanged — October 55.5 is the current monthly reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 103.19 as of November 13, 2026 (DealPlexus: 103.18 up 0.26%; CNBC: 103.189; 52-week high set November 12 at 103.24); DXY extended gains from the November 10 hot-CPI surge (prior: 103.02 Nov 12), cementing December FOMC hike expectations; 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 10 to 103.19 on November 13, net +~1.4–1.7%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted — ICE spot corroborated via DealPlexus and CNBC.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.78% on November 10, 2026 (Goodman Macro daily note; Nov 9: 2.66% per Macrotrends H.15 data, Nov 6: 2.63%, Nov 5: 2.60%); Nov 10 saw a hot-CPI-driven jump of +12bps from 2.66% → 2.78%; 4-week trend remains DOWN — from ~2.85–2.90% around October 10 (2026 high: 2.95% on Oct 5) to 2.78% on November 10, approximately -7 to -12bps net; status supportive (4-week trend down — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2% simultaneously; value is above 2% but 4-week trend still net down, only one condition met); FRED API network-restricted — confirmed via Goodman Macro and Macrotrends corroboration.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at +25bps as of November 10, 2026 (yieldcurve.pro: +25bps Nov 10, down 7bps on day; stockmarketwatch: 25bp; note: sofrrate.com shows 32bps, recessionpulse shows 35bps — diverging trackers); Nov 13 data not yet published; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +28–32bps around October 10 to +25bps on November 10, net change -3 to -7bps within or just at the flat threshold; 52-week range 20–74bps; hot October CPI on Nov 10 drove the 2Y yield up ~17bps, flattening the curve from ~32bps to 25bps intraday; status neutral (positive spread, no steepening trend, not deeply inverted).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,748,145M ($6.748T) for week ended November 4, 2026 (FRED via govspending.org; weekly change +$2.51B WoW, +$175.41B YoY); H.4.1 for week ended November 11, 2026 was released November 12 but exact November 11 figure not retrievable in this run (federalreserve.gov and FRED API both network-restricted); prior readings: Nov 4 $6,748,145M, Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week oscillation range ~$10B band, essentially flat; balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +2.4%; status supportive (flat, no aggressive QT); value held at $6.75T pending confirmation of November 11 H.4.1 figure.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC perp funding rate 0.0098% (~10.8% annualized) as of November 13, 2026 05:36 UTC (CoinGlass price page); CoinGlass futures page (Nov 12 updated) showed OI-weighted rate at 0.0069% (~7.59% annualized, BTC OI $50.91B down 3.15% in 24h); prior readings: 0.0045% (Nov 12 01:51 UTC+8), 0.0063% (Nov 11), 0.0087% (Nov 8); BTC down 4.26% in 24h at $71,469 on Nov 13 with $283.43M in liquidations (96% longs); Fear & Greed at 29 (Fear); US spot ETF net outflows $299.80M on Nov 11; 30-day trend FLAT — mid-October rates were near zero/slightly negative, now 0.0098%, modest uplift but well within neutral range; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold); despite intraday selloff, low funding confirms absence of speculative excess — consistent with accumulation.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $288.1B as of November 11, 2026 (Token Terminal); CoinGecko Nov 8 stablecoin dominance 10.90%; with BTC falling 4.26% on Nov 13 and TOTAL declining to ~$2.41T (BTC at $71,469, BTC.D ~59%), implied stablecoin dominance has ticked up to ~11.9%; 30-day trend UP — October 13 dominance ~10.5–10.8%, rising as TOTAL declined while stablecoins held near $288–295B; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL declined from ~$2.60T (Nov 12) to ~$2.41T (Nov 13), so headwind condition not met; supportive condition (falling dominance) not met either; stablecoin supply has contracted ~$21B from May 2026 peak (~$310B); Tether $179.9B, USDC $71.2B dominate supply.

upcoming.title: US Retail Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey at 8:30 AM ET; September retail sales were +0.8% MoM (well above the +0.3% forecast); a print above +0.5% MoM would add to the already-strong December 9 hike case after the hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM); a miss near 0% would add soft-landing ambiguity but is unlikely to outweigh the inflation surprise given DXY at 52-week highs; this is the last major growth read before the December 9 FOMC decision (FOMC blackout period begins ~November 28).

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases October 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17) at 9:15 AM ET; September industrial production rose +0.4% MoM; a continued expansion would corroborate the October ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); Fed plans an annual G.17 revision release on November 24, so this reading may be subject to revision.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 New Residential Construction at 8:30 AM ET; elevated mortgage rates (30Y near 7.1%) and real yields at 2.66% (down from 2.90% but historically high) continue to pressure housing affordability; after the hot CPI print sealing higher-for-longer expectations, a sharp drop in permits would underscore the housing drag on Q4 2026 growth.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes — October 27–28 Meeting
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% (vote 10–2) at that meeting; minutes will reveal member views on the threshold for a December 9 hike given elevated ISM Prices Paid (75.2 in October, 77.9 in September) and Iran-war supply shocks; the November 10 hot CPI print (+0.4% MoM) and today's October PPI both arrived after the October meeting, so markets will read the minutes against the new inflation reality; PPI data released this morning (Nov 13) adds immediate context; FOMC blackout period begins ~November 28.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET on Thursday November 19; final weekly labor read before Thanksgiving and the ~November 28 FOMC blackout period; a sustained trend above 220K would pressure December 9 hike odds given the already-hot CPI (+0.4% MoM Oct) and elevated DXY; next NFP release is December 4 (November data), arriving just 5 days before the December 9 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia releases November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey at 8:30 AM ET; provides a first-look at November manufacturing activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a positive print above 0 would reinforce the October ISM signal at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); released on the third Thursday of the month.

upcoming.title: Existing Home Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: National Association of Realtors releases October 2026 Existing Home Sales at 10:00 AM ET; mortgage rates near 7.1% continue to suppress turnover via the low-rate lock-in effect; provides a full-month housing transaction count for October; watch for any inventory normalization trends given elevated rate environment.
